ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. Maximum achievable legal-reasoning correctness under H1-H8 is: provable soundness AND completeness of every emitted legal conclusion with respect to IDEAL / SCEPTICAL-PREFERRED CERTIFIED ACCEPTANCE over an explicitly committed, finite, defeasible rulebase — the strongest per-query-unique, deterministic, decidable, certificate-carrying acceptance relation available — where (a) every conclusion carries a machine-checkable certificate re-verifiable offline (H5/H8): for grounded-rung conclusions a finite well-founded derivation tree, for ideal/sceptical-preferred conclusions a certified exhaustive-extension certificate (the complete preferred-extension set, or a refutation-complete search trace) checkable offline with zero producer trust; (b) defeater sensitivity is total over the committed rulebase (every admitted defeater that attacks a derivation is guaranteed to defeat or be defeated in the labelling, including cyclic attack structures); (c) every question whose answer depends on unformalized or interpretively contested source text returns typed UNKNOWN (H2). The grounded (well-founded) extension is the maximal TRACTABLE-UNIQUE rung — the unique semantics that is simultaneously per-query-unique, deterministic, polynomial-time, and certificate-carrying — and grounded acceptance is a STRICT SUBSET of ideal acceptance (recorded gap: even attack cycles occurring in real norm-conflict structures, which ideal semantics may decide and grounded leaves undefined). Restricting operation to the grounded rung is a RESOURCE (cost-class) choice governed by an AX-17 certified cost budget — never a possibility bound. No feasible system can additionally guarantee correctness of the natural-language-to-rule formalization step itself, nor resolve genuinely contested interpretation.
derivation: (1) Computability, stated honestly. Full first-order defeasible logic is undecidable. CREDULOUS acceptance under preferred/stable semantics is non-unique per query, so credulous SELECTION without a committed tie-break breaks H5 — but that argument does not generalize: sceptical acceptance under preferred semantics, and the ideal and eager semantics (Dung-Mancarella-Toni), are (i) per-query UNIQUE and deterministic (H5 replay holds — computing the full extension set or the unique ideal extension is a total pure function of the frozen rulebase), (ii) decidable on the finite committed rulebase (H3 fail-closed termination holds), (iii) certificate-carrying with finite offline-checkable certificates. What they cost is only the complexity class (co-NP-hard verification vs P-time), and polynomial time is not an H1-H8 invariant anywhere in the freeze — cost is exactly what AX-17 certified budgets govern. The v1 lemma 'grounded is the unique maximal semantics' is therefore corrected: grounded is the unique maximum AMONG TRACTABLE unique-status semantics; ideal/sceptical-preferred certified acceptance is the strictly stronger H1-H8-conforming ceiling, strictly containing grounded acceptance. Per the supreme law the stronger conception IS the ceiling; grounded is its tractable rung, retained by declared cost budget only. (2) Information theory: the bytes of a statute underdetermine legal meaning (open texture; contested interpretation is not a computable function of committed text), so correctness about 'the law itself' is not machine-decidable by ANY system; the supremum is correctness relative to a committed formal rulebase plus honest UNKNOWN at the formalization boundary. (3) H1 closes the only escape hatch: a statistical model cannot be trusted to certify the NL-to-formal mapping, so that mapping enters only as attested, admitted input whose certificate records who/what asserted it. Exceeding this restated ceiling requires deciding an undecidable question or a question not encoded in the committed inputs.
ceiling_kind: MODEL_RELATIVE (semantics-relative); the grounded-only restriction inside it is RESOURCE_BOUNDED (AX-17 cost class), never a possibility bound
relativity_note: Relative to the formal argumentation semantics of finite defeasible rule systems: the ceiling names ideal / sceptical-preferred acceptance (Dung-Mancarella-Toni; sceptical acceptance over the complete preferred-extension set) as the acceptance relation, with the grounded/well-founded extension (Dung; Van Gelder-Ross-Schlipf well-founded model) as the tractable-unique rung, grounded STRICTLY CONTAINED in ideal. Correctness claims are meaningful only against the committed formal semantics of the admitted rulebase, never against 'the law' as natural-language text.
lean_obligation: Given a finite attack/support graph G = (N, just), define the alternating-fixpoint operator Phi on labellings L : N -> {in, out, undefined}. Prove: (T1) Phi has a unique least fixpoint wf(G) computed in <= |N| rounds (termination + uniqueness, deterministic replay); (T2) soundness — every node labelled in possesses a finite well-founded derivation tree all of whose defeaters are labelled out; (T3) completeness — every node in the well-founded model is labelled in; (T4) defeater sensitivity — adding any admitted defeater d attacking node n either flips n to out/undefined or yields a certificate that d is itself out; (T5) UNKNOWN monotonicity — undefined never satisfies the acceptance predicate; (T6) ideal-rung theorems — the ideal extension ideal(G) is unique, deterministic, and decidable over finite G; grounded(G) is a subset of ideal(G); exhibit a finite even-cycle witness graph with grounded(G) strictly contained in ideal(G) (the recorded gap); the exhaustive-extension certificate checker accepts a certificate iff it enumerates exactly the preferred extensions of G. All statements are about total functions on finite structures, formalizable in Lean 4.

ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. Maximum achievable plan-decomposition assurance under H1-H8 is: for a plan that is a DETERMINISTIC DERIVATION FROM FROZEN INPUTS (a pure function of the committed closure — pre-commitment of the plan artifact is one sufficient realization, not a necessity) into a finite, explicitly typed dataflow DAG with a declared goal-artifact set, ALL defects in the decidable defect class — cyclic dependency, produces/consumes artifact-type mismatch on any edge, goal artifact unreachable from admitted inputs, orphan stage feeding no goal, ambiguous execution order — are made structurally inadmissible at plan-derivation time (fail-closed, H3); the admitted plan has a unique deterministic total schedule (H5); the plan carries a certificate any third party re-derives from the committed inputs alone (H8); AND the decidable class extends to declared-finite-domain planning: VAL-class precondition/effect validation of a candidate plan against a committed finite-domain action model, and sound+complete plan SYNTHESIS over committed finite domains emitting existence certificates (a valid plan with its validation trace) or nonexistence certificates (an exhaustive refutation over the finite state space). No feasible system can additionally verify completeness of the plan relative to informal human intent, nor decide plan existence over unbounded action spaces.
derivation: (1) Verification theory: completeness relative to intent is not computable — the intent is not encoded; only completeness relative to a committed formal goal specification is machine-checkable (same underdetermination as AX-01). (2) Complexity, corrected: general plan synthesis is PSPACE-complete over finite STRIPS domains and undecidable over infinite domains — but PSPACE-completeness is a cost fact, not an impossibility: over a COMMITTED FINITE domain, plan validation is linear-time decidable and plan existence/synthesis is decidable with checkable certificates, so the feasible decidable class strictly exceeds the five structural DAG checks; the ceiling includes finite-domain synthesis-with-certificates, with cost governed by AX-17 budgets. H5 requires the plan be a PURE FUNCTION of frozen inputs — 'committed before execution' is a sufficient discipline, not the requirement itself: a deterministic planner over a committed finite domain yields replayable synthesized plans that satisfy H5/H6 identically. Against a committed finite DAG, every structural property in the defect class is decidable in O(V+E) with linear-time-checkable certificates; therefore FULL exclusion of the decidable class, not statistical reduction, is feasible — elimination of the error class is the ceiling, guarding against instances is below it. (3) Determinism: among valid schedules, uniqueness is achievable at zero cost (topological sort with total lexicographic tie-break); any nondeterministic schedule strictly violates H5. Exceeding this ceiling requires deciding intent (not encoded) or verifying unbounded plan spaces (undecidable).
relativity_note: Relative to a committed typed-DAG plan semantics (finite stages with declared produces/consumes artifact types and a declared goal-artifact set) extended by a committed finite-domain action model for validation/synthesis. 'Plan completeness' is completeness w.r.t. the committed goal set and domain — never w.r.t. unformalized intent. Witness instantiation: appendix.
lean_obligation: Model a plan as P = (S : Finset Stage, produces, consumes, goals, inputs) with edge relation E s t := (produces s intersect consumes t).Nonempty. Prove: (T1) gate soundness+completeness — the admission predicate wf P holds iff acyclicity, exact type-matching on every edge, goal reachability from inputs, and no orphan stage; (T2) schedule uniqueness — for wf P the tie-broken topological sort is the UNIQUE linearization satisfying the spec; (T3) certificate faithfulness — cert(P) verifies iff wf P; (T4) goal completeness — wf P implies every goal artifact has a finite derivation path from admitted inputs; (T5) planner determinism and certificates — for a committed finite-domain model D, the synthesis function synth : D -> Option Plan is a pure total function; synth D = some p implies valid D p (existence certificate checks), and synth D = none implies an exhaustive-refutation certificate over the finite reachable state space (nonexistence checkable). All over Finset/List with decidable predicates — Lean 4 formalizable.

ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. Maximum achievable contradiction/uncertainty/coverage/blind-spot handling under H1-H8 is certified totality over FOUR verdict classes: every query against the committed corpus and rulebase returns exactly one of {PASS with recomputable certificate; FAIL/CONTRADICTION with recomputable counter-certificate; PASS/FAIL-STABLE-OVER-UNKNOWNS — a KNOWN verdict derived over UNKNOWN inputs carrying a certified invariance (stability) certificate proving the verdict identical under ALL completions of the unknown inputs; typed UNKNOWN carrying a machine-readable reason drawn from a CLOSED, committed enumeration of unknowability causes} — where (a) contradiction detection is provably complete WITHIN a declared decidable class over the committed inputs, (b) the boundary of that class is itself a committed, certificate-carrying, machine-enforced artifact (not prose), (c) coverage is a positively-proven census (absence of a check is itself a detectable, blocking state — no silent gap), and (d) UNKNOWN propagates to every derived fact EXCEPT one carrying a certified invariance (stability) proof that its value is identical under all completions of the unknown input — the input itself remains UNKNOWN, the derived verdict is KNOWN-with-stability-certificate, and absence of such a certificate leaves the derived fact UNKNOWN, terminal, never defaulted to pass/equality (H2), with any flagged anomaly a blocking, non-servable state (H3). No feasible system can additionally certify the absence of unknown-unknowns outside its committed input set, or decide consistency of theories beyond its declared decidable class.
derivation: (1) Computability: consistency of an unrestricted first-order theory is undecidable (and by Goedel II an expressive consistent system cannot prove its own consistency), so 'detects all contradictions' is impossible simpliciter; the supremum is completeness within a declared decidable class plus a checkable declaration of that class's boundary. (2) Information theory: blind spots over inputs never received are undetectable in principle; the ceiling for blind-spot handling is 'no SILENT blind spots over the committed universe': a positively-proven coverage census in which every element of the committed corpus is checked-with-certificate or explicitly enumerated as unchecked. (3) H8: a declared all-clear can never exceed what an independent recomputation over committed inputs establishes. (4) Stability carve-out, corrected from v1: UNCONDITIONAL propagation of UNKNOWN is strictly below the attainable maximum. Certified invariance discharge — three-valued Kleene evaluation, exhaustive case-split, exact stability computation — soundly derives a KNOWN verdict over UNKNOWN inputs whenever the verdict is invariant over ALL completions of the unknown (trivially A or True = True for unknown A; non-trivially a verdict stable over all completions of an unknown dimension). This is not guessing: the certificate quantifies over completions and is offline-recheckable (H2 intact), deterministic (H5), and fail-closed (no invariance certificate, UNKNOWN stands). Without this carve-out a derived verdict provably invariant to an unknown would be withheld — an information-destroying rule, and one that would block tournament verdicts on pairs whose outcome is invariant to the unknown axis. Where evidence about an external candidate supports only a KNOWN_UPPER_BOUND cap rather than a rank, the derived verdict class is the cap, never a rank (see freeze v2). The whole argument is model-independent for any H1-H8 system.
lean_obligation: Fix a finite committed universe U, a finite check family C, a decidable conflict predicate, and a closed inductive type UnknownReason. Define Verdict := pass Cert | fail Cert | stablePass StabCert | stableFail StabCert | unknown UnknownReason. Prove: (T1) totality — the verdict function V is total; (T2) certificate soundness — pass/fail certificates re-verify under the independent checker; (T3) in-class completeness — every conflicting rule pair in the committed rulebase yields fail with a counter-certificate naming the pair; (T4) census positivity — for every (c,u) in C x U the coverage matrix contains exactly one of {checked-with-cert, enumerated-unchecked}, a missing entry unrepresentable in the manifest type; (T5) UNKNOWN terminality with the stability carve-out — no function in the trusted API maps unknown r to pass; the only KNOWN verdict derivable over an unknown input is stablePass/stableFail, and (T6) stability soundness — stablePass sc implies for ALL completions f of the unknown inputs, V under f = pass (and dually for stableFail); the certificate checker verifies exactly this quantification over the finite completion space. All over finite decidable structures, Lean 4 formalizable.

ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. For any system satisfying H1-H8, the maximum attainable grounding of a served legal text t is: (i) ORIGIN AUTHENTICITY no stronger than what can be TRANSPORTED, CORROBORATED, or CHANNEL-ATTESTED — (a) transport: verification of the official publisher's cryptographic signature over the captured bytes, bounded by the publisher's PKI; (b) corroboration: agreement of a k-of-n quorum of independent, contemporaneous capture witnesses over the byte digest, whose assurance is a MONOTONE FUNCTION of the declared witness set's size and independence — a resource-parameterized bound with no absolute maximum; (c) attested-channel capture: a TLS-oracle protocol (DECO/TLSNotary-class) or TEE-attested fetcher binding the received bytes to the publisher's TLS channel identity at capture time, transporting origin assurance through the publisher's channel key where the content is unsigned, at the cost of the respective protocol or hardware-vendor trust anchor; anything below these is admissible only as typed UNKNOWN/provisional. NEGATIVE HALF (the only ABSOLUTE clause): no local computation over already-held bytes can create origin authenticity after the fact — a digest commits to WHAT was received, never to WHO published it. Plus (ii) DERIVATION BINDING — a deterministic, third-party re-executable extraction function E with byte-equality E(captured-bytes) = t, committed as a dual digest; plus (iii) CORPUS-SIZE INDEPENDENCE — Grounded(t) mentions only the committed capture record of t's own source (selection by exact committed identifier, never by search/glob/statistics), invariant under corpus extension, with membership verification O(log n) via Merkle inclusion — optimal among hash-based schemes with no setup assumptions (constant-size membership proofs exist under other assumption families, e.g. RSA accumulators and vector commitments, at the cost of those assumptions).
derivation: The negative half is information-theoretic and model-independent: authenticity of bytes fetched from a network endpoint cannot be created after the fact by any local computation. The POSITIVE mechanisms number three, not two (v1 corrected): (a) signature transport — a key predating the capture, rooted in the publisher; (b) independent corroboration — k witnesses on disjoint trust/network paths committing the same digest at capture time, forgery requiring compromise of all k or the endpoint itself, with assurance monotone in the declared witness set (hence resource-parameterized, no absolute cap); (c) attested-channel capture — origin assurance transported through the publisher's TLS channel identity via an oracle protocol or attested fetcher, strictly stronger than a bare single-witness digest and independent of (a) and (b), introducing a protocol/hardware trust anchor of the same category as the genesis anchors AX-12 accepts. H1 forbids substituting a statistical model's authenticity judgment; H8 forbids trusting the producer's declared root. Part (ii): 'served text derives from primary bytes' is zero-trust checkable only for a pure deterministic derivation compared byte-for-byte — the ceiling is deterministic-replay equality. Part (iii): any grounding predicate consulting corpus-global state breaks replay under corpus growth and adds zero authenticity; O(log n) Merkle inclusion suffices and is optimal among hash-based, setup-free schemes.
ceiling_kind: ABSOLUTE (negative half: no after-the-fact authenticity) / RESOURCE_BOUNDED (positive clauses: publisher PKI, witness-set parameterization, attested-channel trust anchors)
relativity_note: The positive origin-assurance clauses are parameterized by declared resources: the publisher's signing practice, the declared witness set (witness networks are operational today — enrolling is a feasible act, not an unreachable resource), and the availability of an attested-channel stack. Only the negative half is model- and resource-independent.
lean_obligation: With hash : Bytes -> Digest collision-resistant (axiom), E : Bytes -> ServedText total computable, sigOK : PublisherKey -> Bytes -> Sig -> Prop, chanOK : ChannelAnchor -> Bytes -> Attestation -> Prop, and a finite witness set W: define Grounded t c := (transport OR quorum(k) OR channel-attested) AND E c.bytes = t. Prove: (T-ceiling) any grounding predicate P satisfying H5 and H8 implies P t -> Grounded t (Grounded is the supremum of the three-mechanism family); (T-negative) no predicate computable from already-held bytes alone, without a transport, quorum, or channel witness, entails origin authenticity — formalized as: for any such P there exist two capture histories with identical held bytes and different true origins that P cannot separate; (T-monotone) quorum assurance is monotone in (k, independence structure of W) — the corroboration bound is a function of the declared witness set, not a constant; (T-attain) the admission predicate equals Grounded; (T-size-indep) for corpora C subset C', Grounded t c holds in C iff in C', and Merkle inclusion verification is O(log |C|).

ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. Relative to a declared decidable citation grammar G for the legal order and a fixed authority-chain semantics, the maximum attainable by any H1-H8 system is: SOUND AND COMPLETE PROOF-CARRYING RESOLUTION OVER L(G) — every string in L(G) occurring in served text is parsed by a total, coverage-gated recognizer and resolved to exactly one committed authority record carrying a verified receipt (signature chain valid to a pinned owner key, delegation valid at the receipt's genTime, revocation checked, bitemporal validity covering the citation's reference time), and every citation-like string outside L(G) is emitted as typed UNKNOWN-CITATION that never upgrades to a pass (H2). SEMANTIC SUPPORT, split honestly (v1 corrected): for propositions that are FORMAL OBJECTS of the system, support-verification is INSIDE the ceiling — derivation provenance makes it decidable: the conclusion's certified derivation uses rule R, whose admission record binds R to a pinpoint span S of authority A, so 'the cited authority is the recorded basis of the citing proposition' is a zero-LLM decidable predicate attained by AX-01 x AX-04 composition. What remains excluded for every feasible system is NL-vs-NL support — verification that a natural-language authority text semantically supports a natural-language proposition — and recognition of arbitrary natural-language reference intent outside G; claiming either without human adjudication is structurally dishonest under H1.
derivation: Computability: the set of NL strings that function as citations has no decidable characterization; any total mechanical recognizer fixes a formal language, so the ceiling is stated relative to a declared decidable G. H1 closes the escape: a statistical model approximating NL intent is banned from the trusted path; its output is an untrusted CANDIDATE re-entering through the G-verifier. Within L(G), verification theory gives the maximum: binding to an authority record whose authenticity chain is checkable offline with zero producer trust (H8) — signature to pinned root, delegation window containment, revocation absence, bitemporal validity — the strongest offline-checkable statement about the citation's TARGET; authority-ness beyond the committed chain reduces to the AX-04 origin ceiling. The semantic-support impossibility is SCOPED (v1 overshoot corrected): it applies to NL-proposition-vs-NL-authority support, which requires an oracle for legal meaning; formal-proposition support reduces to derivation provenance over committed admission records — decidable, inside the ceiling. Consistency: the JWS layer proves internal consistency, not authenticity; authenticity enters only through the pinned-owner chain.
relativity_note: Relative to: (1) a declared decidable citation grammar G for the legal order; (2) a TUF-style delegation semantics with owner-key pinning; (3) a bitemporal validity semantics (valid-time x transaction-time with a genTime floor). Change any of the three and the ceiling statement changes with it. Witness instantiation (Greek FEK/ELI grammar and the B0 seats): appendix.
lean_obligation: Fix G with decidable membership, receipts R with decidable chainValid and validAt predicates over committed bytes, resolve : {s // s in L G} -> Option R pure, out : String -> Result total. Prove: (SOUND) out s = .cited r implies s in L G and resolve s = some r and chainValid r and validAt r (refTime s); (COMPLETE-rel-G) every s in L G yields a verified receipt or a typed failure, never silence; (HONEST) s not in L G implies out s = .unknown, and .unknown never coerces to .cited (type-level H2); (SUPPORT-formal) for a formal conclusion c with certified derivation d, supports(A, c) is decidable: it holds iff some rule R in d has an admission record binding R to a committed span S of A — soundness and completeness of this predicate w.r.t. the derivation semantics; (CEILING) any output function under H1/H5/H8 claiming .cited on s not in L G contradicts decidability of the trusted path.

ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. The maximum evidence-provenance and transformation-lineage ASSURANCE attainable by any H1-H8 system is: the verifier's knowledge of an artifact's lineage is bounded by what is derivable from committed bytes under stated cryptographic assumptions — attained by PER-STEP VERIFICATION OVER A COMMITTED PURE-TRANSFORMATION DAG, TOTAL OVER THE RELEASE CLOSURE, where each step (input-hash, deterministic-transformation-id, output-hash) is committed under a domain-separated Merkle root bound inside the signed release identity, and per-step verification is performed by either of two EQUALLY MAXIMAL modes under the same hash-assumption family: (a) recompute-and-compare (re-execute the declared transformation, compare output bytes), or (b) checking a transparent proof-of-recomputation (STARK-class: no trusted setup, soundness resting on hash/collision-resistance assumptions of the same family as the SHA-256 commitments). Any artifact lacking a complete chain, or any step failing verification, blocks the release (fail-closed totality). Assurance is bounded exactly by (i) collision resistance of the commitment hash, (ii) purity/determinism of each declared step, (iii) the AX-04 origin ceiling at the chain's roots. COST clause (RESOURCE_BOUNDED): linear-cost recompute is the operative verification floor only for a declared toolchain lacking an arithmetization of its pipeline; a transparent proof toolchain strictly lowers verification cost with no assurance loss, and succinct proofs for update-validity predicates over bounded structures are implemented today.
derivation: (1) Information-theoretic: un-committed history is unrecoverable — a verifier establishes facts only about data committed at production time; an aggregate base-hash/result-hash + step-count provably admits distinct histories with identical aggregates, so aggregate-only lineage sits strictly below the ceiling; per-step commitment is the maximum granularity of verifiable lineage. (2) Verification theory, corrected from v1: H8's semantic content is ZERO PRODUCER TRUST, not a privileged verification procedure — deriving 'recompute-and-compare is the ceiling' from H8-as-recompute would restate an axiom, not prove a limit. Under zero producer trust the verifier accepts exactly what is derivable from committed bytes under stated assumptions; both recompute-and-compare AND transparent proof-of-recomputation meet that bar under the SAME assumption family (the v1 dismissal of proof mode rested on a false trusted-setup premise — STARK-class systems have none). Recompute-and-compare is SUFFICIENT for the assurance ceiling; it is NOT NECESSARY (the v1 'necessary and sufficient' is deleted). An impure or nondeterministic step is unverifiable offline in either mode, so the ceiling covers exactly the pure-step DAG, with anything else typed UNKNOWN (H2). (3) Completeness is a closure property: totality over a finite committed set is decidable by census, so a fail-closed census gate attains the maximum. The former absolute Omega(s) recomputation floor is DELETED from the assurance claim and restated as the cost clause: it binds only the recompute mode on a proof-less toolchain — a resource fact, never part of an ABSOLUTE label.
ceiling_kind: ABSOLUTE (assurance-semantics clause, under stated hash assumptions) / RESOURCE_BOUNDED (cost clause)

ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. For any feasible system under H1-H8, institutional/reflective memory can guarantee at most: (a) provenance-complete capture — every certified state transition (H6) is committed as an episode carrying content digests of all inputs that decided it, so each remembered decision is offline-replayable (H5); (b) tamper-evidence by full recomputation over EPISODE COMMITMENTS — an offline verifier holding only the log bytes recomputes the whole hash chain from canonical episode commitments and detects any mutation, deletion, insertion, or reorder, up to hash collision-resistance (H8); the commitment layer admits salted per-leaf commitments (chain over H(salt || body)) so that verifiable-redaction/erasure certificates can destroy a body or salt while chain verification and inclusion proofs survive — reconciling complete tamper-evidence with lawful-erasure duties, with every redaction carrying a typed erasure certificate, never silent deletion; (c) rollback/fork detection exactly relative to the verifier's freshest previously-held committed checkpoint (prefix-consistency against any held prior head) — the fork-consistency bound, liftable by a live external witness quorum, WHICH IS A DEPLOYMENT RESOURCE, NOT AN IMPOSSIBILITY (witness networks are operational today); (d) recall as a pure deterministic function of the committed prefix, with typed UNKNOWN for anything never committed (H2). No feasible system can remember what was not committed at event time, or produce a producer-trust-free proof of its own live in-RAM state WITHOUT introducing a hardware trust anchor (TEE remote attestation relocates the anchor to the hardware vendor — the same category of irreducible anchor as a genesis key — it does not eliminate it).
derivation: (1) Information-theoretic no-retrodiction: memory at time t is a function of bytes committed by t; an uncommitted observation is absent from every later verification; H2 forces UNKNOWN rather than reconstruction. (2) Fork-consistency bound (Mazieres-Shasha / SUNDR): with an untrusted producer and a verifier whose only input is the log bytes, two distinct well-formed histories are indistinguishable — internal consistency is verifiable, 'this is THE history' is not; the escapes are a verifier-held prior checkpoint (prefix-consistency relative to that floor) or an external witness quorum. The quorum clause is RESOURCE_BOUNDED, not absolute (v1 corrected): by the same labeling standard as AX-21, a resource that would strictly lift the cap and is excluded only by declared deployment scope makes the clause resource-bounded — and cross-ecosystem witness networks with shared vetted log configurations operate today, so enrolling is a feasible act. (3) Self-verification limit, reworded: a process cannot produce a producer-trust-free proof of its own live runtime state without a hardware trust anchor; with TEE attestation the trust relocates to the vendor anchor. Within these bounds, a single canonical serialization point (physical single writer, or machine-checked nonforking logical writer — H4) plus hash chaining with the chain discipline sealed inside the hashed commitment attains every guarantee the limits permit. Whether any given implementation attains it is an attainment hypothesis for the appendix — the frozen derivation bounds, it does not certify attainment.
ceiling_kind: ABSOLUTE (clauses a, b, d; no-retrodiction; anchored self-attestation limit) / RESOURCE_BOUNDED (clause c fork-consistency cap, liftable by an external witness quorum — an operationally available resource)
relativity_note: The erasure-compatible commitment layer in clause (b) is a lattice-refinement of v1 recorded per S2 discipline: 'complete tamper-evidence over bodies' and 'lawful erasure' cannot both rank as previously worded; commitments-with-typed-redaction is the reconciling form.

ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. For any feasible system under H1-H8, temporal and legal-state consistency can guarantee at most: (a) gapless monotone history — every admitted transition satisfies seq' = seq + 1 exactly, serialized through a single canonical serialization point (physical single-writer admission, or a machine-checked nonforking replicated total order), so system history is a certificate-carrying total order with no gaps, repeats, or rollback (H4/H6); (b) append-only verifiability — any verifier holding any prior committed root verifies by recomputing a consistency proof that the current log extends it; a verifier with no prior root can verify internal consistency only (wholesale replacement undetectable to a fresh verifier — the fork-consistency bound), liftable by an external witness quorum, which is a DEPLOYMENT RESOURCE available today, not an impossibility; (c) bitemporal legal-state soundness — 'legal state at valid-time t as known at transaction-time tau' is at most a pure, offline-replayable function (H5/H8) of the source snapshots and typed amendment events committed by tau under a declared formal amendment semantics, returning typed UNKNOWN (H2) for any (t, tau) not covered by committed evidence. No feasible system can assert legal state beyond its committed evidence, anticipate unpublished amendments, or exceed checkpoint-relative anti-rollback without external witnesses.
derivation: (1) Evidence bound: at transaction-time tau the system possesses exactly its committed bytes; an issued-but-uncaptured amendment is informationally absent; H1/H2 forbid statistical interpolation, forcing typed UNKNOWN. (2) Purity bound: H5 + H8 require the (t, tau) view to be recomputable by a third party from committed inputs alone; the deterministic bitemporal view over committed snapshots IS the ceiling. (3) Fork-consistency bound (Mazieres-Shasha): the transparency log alone proves internal append-only consistency; distinguishing the true history from a consistent fabrication requires a verifier-held prior root (prefix theorem via consistency proofs) or a cosigning witness quorum — the quorum sub-clause is RESOURCE_BOUNDED (witness networks operate today; enrollment is a feasible act), so consumer-floor-relative anti-rollback is the maximum only for a deployment declining that resource. (4) Serialization bound, restated without the single-authority assumption baked in: exactly-once gapless sequence increment requires one logical serialization point; a physical single-writer kernel attains it directly; a machine-checked nonforking replicated total order (partially-synchronous BFT-class consensus) attains it with operator-independence at declared consensus-resource cost — deterministic consensus impossibility (FLP) binds only the fully asynchronous faulty model and does not cap either route. In-force/implicit-repeal determinations are interpretation-laden, which is why clause (c) is definable only relative to a named formal amendment semantics.
ceiling_kind: MODEL_RELATIVE (clause c) / ABSOLUTE (clause a; clause b internal-consistency half, under hash assumptions) / RESOURCE_BOUNDED (clause b anti-rollback-beyond-held-floor half — witness quorum)
relativity_note: Clause (c) is relative to a declared bitemporal amendment semantics: transaction-time = admission sequence of the Merkle-committed corpus; valid-time = publisher-declared in-force intervals; amendment effects = typed events (repeal, substitution, insertion) applied by an explicit event calculus over FRBR/Akoma-Ntoso-style versioning. The v1 note labeling sub-bound (b) ABSOLUTE outright is corrected: its witness-conditioned half carries the same RESOURCE_BOUNDED carve-out as AX-07(c) and AX-12's equivocation clause.

(Tightness) exhibit two distinct well-formed logs both satisfying internal consistency — a fresh verifier cannot separate them, establishing that the anti-rollback half beyond a held floor strictly requires an external witness resource.
